generated_from: Mullins Seven Domains of Attractive Opportunities (Phase 84-04, v1.10.8)

sections.title: Market Size Today
sections.prompt: How large is the addressable market right now in units, customers, and dollars?

sections.title: Market Size in Five Years
sections.prompt: How large will the addressable market be five years out, and what drives that growth?

sections.title: Market-Level Benefits
sections.prompt: What benefits does this market deliver that customers cannot easily get elsewhere?

sections.title: Macro Trends
sections.prompt: Which macro trends make this market more or less attractive over the planning horizon?

sections.title: Political and Regulatory Climate
sections.prompt: What political, legal, and regulatory forces shape this market's attractiveness?

sections.title: Economic Cycles
sections.prompt: How sensitive is this market to economic cycles, interest rates, and capital availability?

sections.title: Social and Cultural Forces
sections.prompt: Which social and cultural shifts pull customers toward or away from this market?

sections.title: Beachhead Segment
sections.prompt: Which narrowly defined customer segment will the venture win first, and why them?

sections.title: Segment-Specific Benefits
sections.prompt: What unique benefits does this segment receive that no incumbent currently delivers?

sections.title: Segment Reachability
sections.prompt: How will the venture reach this segment economically and at scale?

sections.title: Competitive Rivalry
sections.prompt: How intense is rivalry among existing competitors in this industry?

sections.title: Supplier Power
sections.prompt: How much bargaining power do suppliers hold over participants in this industry?

sections.title: Buyer Power
sections.prompt: How much bargaining power do buyers hold, and how price-sensitive are they?

sections.title: Barriers to Entry
sections.prompt: What barriers protect insiders from new entrants, and which ones can the venture build?

sections.title: Substitute Threats
sections.prompt: What substitutes could replace this industry's offering and at what cost?

sections.title: Team Mission
sections.prompt: What is the founding team's mission and why is this team the one to pursue it?

sections.title: Team Aspirations
sections.prompt: What outcomes does the team aspire to over the next three to seven years?

sections.title: Propensity for Risk
sections.prompt: How much risk is the team willing and able to absorb, and across which dimensions?

sections.title: Critical Success Factors
sections.prompt: Which few things must go right for this venture to succeed, and how will the team ensure them?

sections.title: Value Chain Connections
sections.prompt: Which upstream, downstream, and lateral relationships in the value chain unlock this venture?

brain_folders.title: Value Proposition
brain_folders.prompt: What precise value does the offering deliver to the beachhead segment, and how is it worth paying for?

brain_folders.title: Disruptive vs Sustaining Posture
brain_folders.prompt: Is this venture sustaining an incumbent trajectory or disrupting from a new-market or low-end foothold?

brain_folders.title: Systems Map
brain_folders.prompt: Which feedback loops, stocks, and leverage points govern this venture as a nested system?

ascent.label: Domain data gathered
ascent.movement: Fill each Mullins domain folder with raw facts, figures, and observations toward Validation-at-center

ascent.label: Domains structured
ascent.movement: Relate the domain data into patterns and answered prompts, climbing toward Validation

ascent.label: Cross-domain connections earned
ascent.movement: Connect the structured domains into a coherent opportunity read, earning evidence up the levels toward Validation

ascent.label: Validation at center
ascent.movement: Resolve the connected domains into a validated go decision at the Validation center -- the ascent confirms confidence is backed

descent.label: Validation decomposes
descent.movement: Begin the New Business Road Test loop: Validation decomposes back to interrogate the validated read

descent.label: Re-test connections
descent.movement: Re-test each cross-domain connection against fresh evidence, pulling back to expose weak couplings

descent.label: Re-test structure
descent.movement: Re-test the structured domains, surfacing assumptions that no longer hold

descent.label: Re-test domain data
descent.movement: Decompose down to re-test each domain's underlying data and assumptions -- the descent re-tests what the ascent earned
